note: Dominant RNU2-2 DEE shows high status epilepticus and older onset (median 24 months), contrasting with predominant infantile spasms in recessive cohorts.

evidence.text: In a study of dominant RNU2-2 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, all 5 patients experienced status epilepticus with median seizure onset at 24 months, presenting with focal and generalized seizures.

source.title: Pathogenic Variants in RNU2‐2, a Non‐coding Spliceosomal RNA, Cause a Distinctive Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
source.quote: Patients with RNU2-2 DEE had median seizure onset age of 24 months, focal and generalized seizures, status epilepticus (n = 5), severe to profound impairment

numbers.metric: median seizure onset age in months

evidence.text: In biallelic recessive RNU2-2 DEE, infantile spasms and tonic seizures were the predominant seizure types, with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome-like features and status epilepticus seen in over half of individuals.

source.title: Phenotypic and transcriptomic characterization of biallelic RNU2‐2 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
source.quote: Infantile spasms and tonic seizures were the predominant seizure types and a Lennox-Gastaut syndrome-like phenotype was common. More than half the cohort had status epilepticus (8/14, 57%)
